environment: Humpback highway peaks as thousands of whales cruise past the Queensland coast on their spring trip south
Volunteers turn out in droves for spring bushcare working bees across the south-east, with native seedlings going in the ground from Redlands to the Sunshine Coast hinterland
science: Queensland marine scientists trial new heat-tolerant coral strains on the Great Barrier Reef ahead of this season's spawning
sports: Queensland clubs gear up for a big September as the NRL finals series kicks off around the state
stories.overview: A southern right whale calf is spotted frolicking with its mum just off the Queensland coast, delighting whale watchers on the first proper spring morning of the year

segments.title: The Open
segments.script: G'day and welcome to ParkSyde Bright Side, I'm Alex Mercer, and mate, it is an absolute cracker of a Wednesday out there. Spring has well and truly sprung across the Sunshine State and we've got a ripper of a show for you. I'm Jamie, and Alex is not wrong, there is something in the air today. We've got whales putting on a show, scientists doing clever things with coral, and footy finals fever building up nicely. Too right. So grab your cuppa, settle in, and let's get into it, because honestly this is one of those episodes where good news just keeps rolling in.

segments.title: Green Desk
segments.script: Let's start on the water, because it is peak whale season along our coast right now. Thousands of humpbacks are cruising past on their way south, and this week a southern right whale calf was spotted having an absolute ball with its mum just off the coast. Love that. There is nothing quite like standing on a headland with a coffee and watching a whale the size of a bus do a tail slap for no reason other than it feels like it. Pure joy, no charge. And it's not just the whales doing their bit for spring. Bushcare crews from Redlands right through to the Sunshine Coast hinterland have been turning out in big numbers for planting days, getting native seedlings in the ground while the weather is kind.

segments.title: Science & Tomorrow
segments.script: Righto, over to the science desk. Queensland marine researchers are trialling new heat tolerant coral strains out on the Great Barrier Reef, getting them ready before the coral spawning kicks off later this season. It's basically giving the reef a bit of a head start against warmer waters, which is exactly the kind of clever, patient science we love to see. Nothing flashy, just years of careful work paying off. Exactly, no lab coat theatrics, just scientists quietly stacking the odds in the reef's favour. We'll definitely keep an eye on how those new corals go when spawning season properly hits.

segments.title: Weather
segments.script: Cheers Alex, thanks for that. Now looking across the south-east, it is shaping up as a beautiful spring day, plenty of sunshine, light winds and top temps sitting in that pleasant low to mid twenties from Brisbane down through the Gold Coast and up to the Sunshine Coast. Overnight lows are still a bit crisp, dipping into the teens, so don't put the doona away just yet. Looking ahead through the rest of the week, we're tracking mostly clear skies with just a chance of a stray afternoon cloud build-up inland, so it is looking like prime time for a walk along the beach or a bit of whale watching from the headlands. Back to you two in the studio.

segments.title: The Scoreboard
segments.script: Righto, footy time, and September means one thing around here, finals fever. Queensland clubs are gearing up for the NRL finals series and you can feel the buzz building in pubs and backyards right across the state. There is nothing like September footy, the tension is next level and everyone suddenly becomes an expert on the eight point try line rule. It is genuinely one of the best times of year to be a sports fan up here. Whatever happens, it is shaping up as a cracking finals series to watch with mates. Get your snacks sorted and enjoy the ride, because this is footy at its business end.

Whales putting on a show, scientists giving the reef a helping hand, and finals footy just around the corner. It really does feel like spring is bringing its A game this year. Big thanks to Sam for the weather and to everyone out there planting trees and getting amongst it this week. Couldn't agree more, Queensland just does spring differently, doesn't it.
